items.title: Democrats secure largest House majority since 1992
items.feedTitle: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, the largest since 1992
items.summary: Democrats have secured at least 258 House seats following their midterm election victories, marking their largest majority in a regular election in three decades. The 258-seat count was finalized after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, with four races still undecided. This gives Democrats control of both chambers of Congress starting in January, setting up a significant shift in legislative power.

items.title: Appeals court voids pregnancy worker accommodation law
items.feedTitle: Appeals court says federal law requiring accommodations for pregnant workers is unconstitutional
items.summary: A federal appeals court ruled that a law requiring accommodations for pregnant workers is unconstitutional, citing that a majority of House members were not physically present when it was approved as part of a December 2022 spending package. The ruling puts at risk workplace protections enacted during the Biden administration, though the decision is likely to face further legal challenges.

items.title: El-Sayed proposes naming Medicare for All 'TrumpCare
items.feedTitle: El-Sayed would pass Medicare for All as 'TrumpCare': 'I don't really care what it's called'
items.summary: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed said he would support passing a single-payer healthcare bill under the name 'TrumpCare' if it secured the president's backing, saying the specific name does not matter as long as the policy passes. The proposal aims to appeal to Trump's ego while advancing Democratic healthcare priorities, reflecting a tactical shift in how the new Senate majority may frame legislation.

items.title: Trump vows to cap credit card interest rates at ten percent
items.feedTitle: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%
items.summary: Trump pledged to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent, a substantial reduction from the median rate of roughly 22.2 percent. The proposal would require congressional action and faces questions about implementation and economic impacts, but signals potential bipartisan effort on consumer finance regulation.

items.title: Army plans emergency detonation of Iowa bomb chemicals
items.feedTitle: US Army plans to invoke emergency provisions to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
items.summary: The U.S. Army plans to invoke emergency provisions to detonate several tons of lead azide, a bomb-making chemical, in Fort Madison, Iowa, despite environmental concerns and a court-ordered stay. The Army says swift action is necessary to protect personnel and nearby communities, but critics argue the government is circumventing court orders and proper safety procedures.

stlouis.title: Missouri woman detained by ICE at St. Louis airport
stlouis.feedTitle: Friend fears for Missouri woman detained by immigration agents at St. Louis airport
stlouis.summary: A Missouri woman was detained by immigration agents at St. Louis Lambert International Airport, prompting concern from friends and civil liberties advocates. The incident raises questions about ICE enforcement actions and their scope within the region, with no immediate details available on the woman's status or the basis for her detention.

stlouis.title: Illegal slot machines returning to Missouri gas stations
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri AG barred illegal slot machines. They're still going back into gas stations.
stlouis.summary: Despite a Missouri attorney general enforcement action to remove illegal slot machines from gas stations, the machines are reportedly being reinstalled in locations across the state. The situation highlights ongoing enforcement challenges and the persistence of illegal gambling operations in the region.

stlouis.title: St. Louis Blues beat New Jersey Devils nine to six
stlouis.feedTitle: Goals galore! Blues beat Devils 9-6 in another high-scoring affair
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis Blues defeated the New Jersey Devils in a high-scoring game, with nine goals for the home team. The match continues the team's competitive season performance.

items.title: Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after drone attack
items.feedTitle: Russian vessel hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Libya’s Benghazi port
items.summary: The Merkury, a Russian navy corvette docked in Benghazi, Libya, was struck by suspected Ukrainian sea drones in early Sunday, causing an explosion and fire that resulted in the ship's sinking. The vessel was docked en route back to Russia after refueling, and no one has claimed responsibility for the attack, though Ukrainian naval operations have targeted Russian assets in distant waters.

items.title: COP31 climate talks collapse over fossil fuels impasse
items.feedTitle: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
items.summary: The UN climate summit in Turkey ended without a major agreement after two weeks of negotiations, as countries remained divided over explicitly mentioning fossil fuels in the final deal. The EU, UK, and developing nations rejected the proposed text, saying it failed to meet the moment and lacked adequate fossil fuel language, marking a significant setback for global climate cooperation.

items.title: Boy, seven, pulled from rubble after Russian strike
items.feedTitle: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
items.summary: Rescue workers in Ukraine pulled a seven-year-old boy alive from rubble hours after a Russian strike on a residential building killed at least nine people. The attack caused a building to collapse in Ukraine's Kyiv region, with rescue efforts ongoing to find others still trapped in the debris.

items.title: Red Cross warns on autonomous weapons regulation
items.feedTitle: It will soon be too late to regulate use of autonomous weapons, warns Red Cross
items.summary: The International Red Cross warns it will soon be too late to regulate the use of autonomous weapons, as development accelerates without international legal frameworks. UN talks on lethal autonomous weapons ended without producing binding agreements, raising concerns that military AI systems will proliferate without adequate oversight or ethical guardrails.

items.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon acted like a ‘poorly behaved boyfriend’ before alleged double murders, defence argues
items.feedTitle: Beau Lamarre-Condon acted like a ‘poorly behaved boyfriend’ before alleged double murders, defence argues
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: India flags climate equity concerns at COP31 collapse
items.feedTitle: COP31 ends without pact as India flags climate equity concerns
items.summary: India emphasized climate equity and developing-world concerns during COP31 negotiations, as the summit ended without a binding agreement. Indian officials stressed that wealthy nations have historically contributed more to climate emissions and bear greater responsibility for climate finance commitments, highlighting the fault lines between developed and developing nations.

items.title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.4% of APL Apollo
items.feedTitle: India's Tata Steel to buy 26.4% of APL Apollo for $1.67 billion
items.summary: India's Tata Steel announced plans to acquire a 26.4 percent stake in APL Apollo for $1.67 billion, signaling continued expansion into related industrial sectors. The move strengthens Tata Steel's portfolio and reflects the conglomerate's strategy for growth in domestic and global markets.

items.title: India-EU free trade deal expected December sixteen
items.feedTitle: India, EU likely to sign long-awaited free trade deal on December 16
items.summary: India and the European Union are likely to sign a long-awaited free trade agreement on December 16 during Prime Minister Modi's visit to Brussels. The pact, under negotiation for years, is expected to boost bilateral commerce and deepen economic ties between the two economic powerhouses.

items.title: India and China hold LAC tensions talks in Arunachal
items.feedTitle: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
items.summary: India and China conducted 10-day talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh, focusing on engagement protocols, preventing face-offs, and maintaining open military communication channels. The diplomatic effort signals both nations' desire to manage border disagreements through dialogue.

items.title: FSSAI prosecutes Bisleri for unsafe drinking water
items.feedTitle: India's food regulator to take Bisleri to court over water quality finding
items.summary: India's food regulator FSSAI ordered prosecution against Bisleri International after finding carcinogenic bromate levels exceeding prescribed limits in packaged drinking water samples. The action highlights concerns over drinking water quality and regulatory oversight of major beverage manufacturers.

immigration.title: Labor Department proposes sweeping PERM overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor proposed a major overhaul of the PERM (Permanent Labor Certification) program, introducing stricter requirements for employers sponsoring foreign workers—proposed, not yet final. Changes include extended recruitment periods, a two-year layoff bar, and elimination of Schedule A fast-track provisions for nurses and other professions, raising concerns from healthcare and tech employers.

immigration.title: Trump green card rules could hurt nursing workforce
immigration.feedTitle: Trump administration’s green card rules would make it harder to hire nurses
immigration.summary: Trump administration proposals to tighten green card rules threaten to make it harder for U.S. hospitals to hire foreign nurses and healthcare workers, as new PERM requirements may restrict employer flexibility—proposed, not yet final. Healthcare advocates warn the changes could worsen existing nursing shortages across the country.

immigration.title: Indian Google engineer leaves U.S. on H-1B visa
immigration.feedTitle: ‘Golden Prison’: Indian Google engineer leaves US after six years on H-1B visa
immigration.summary: An Indian engineer working for Google on an H-1B visa decided to relocate to the UK without securing another job, citing the U.S. as a 'golden prison' due to visa constraints and immigration uncertainty. The move reflects growing frustration among skilled migrants over delayed visa processing and shifting policy landscape affecting work authorization.

items.title: Tech stock sell-off deepens in Asia amid AI rout
items.feedTitle: Tech stock sell-off deepens in Asia
items.summary: Asian stock markets tumbled as the artificial intelligence sector sell-off deepened, with indices in South Korea, Taiwan, mainland China, and Hong Kong declining sharply. The rout erased earlier gains and raised concerns about whether the AI investment boom had been overheated, triggering a broader market correction.

items.title: U.S. futures surge after worst tech selloff since 2020
items.feedTitle: Nasdaq futures surge nearly 3%, S&P 500 futures jump over 2% after worst tech selloff since 2020
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures rebounded significantly, with Nasdaq futures surging nearly 3 percent and S&P 500 futures jumping over 2 percent, following the worst technology-led selloff since 2020. The bounce suggests investor relief and potential stabilization, though volatility is expected to persist.

items.title: India's Nifty stands apart amid global stock selloff
items.feedTitle: India’s Nifty Stands Apart as Global Stocks, Gold Suffer Rare Joint Selloff
items.summary: While global equities and precious metals suffered rare joint losses, India's Nifty index outperformed, supported by strong foreign portfolio investor buying and domestic market resilience. The divergence highlights India's attractiveness as investors seek non-tech exposure amid AI sector uncertainty.

items.title: Trump blames six-trillion-dollar market slide on Democrats
items.feedTitle: Trump Says $6 Trillion Stock Market Wipeout Is "100% the Democrats' Fault"; Bessent Points to a Mix of Factors
items.summary: President Trump attributed the stock market's $6 trillion decline to Democrats' midterm election victories, claiming their new congressional control created uncertainty. Treasury Secretary Bessent offered a more nuanced view, citing multiple factors including AI sector valuations and geopolitical tensions.

items.title: Judge approves seven-point-two-five-billion Roundup settlement
items.feedTitle: Judge approves $7.25bn Bayer payout to settle claims that Roundup causes cancer
items.summary: A Missouri federal judge approved Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement resolving approximately 65,000 lawsuits alleging that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. The settlement represents a major resolution of litigation that has weighed on the German company for years, though it does not constitute an admission of liability.

finance.note: Oil prices fell as broad equity sell-off deepened, though Iran tensions provided some floor to losses; U.S. stock futures rebounded 2–3% after the worst tech rout since 2020, while Asian markets remained under pressure. India's Nifty and Sensex are bucking the trend with strong FPI inflows. Watch for FOMC communications this week, Thanksgiving-related trading volume, and whether the AI sector stabilizes or faces further correction.

cards.title: Constraints birth breakthroughs
cards.insight: Creative solutions emerge not from unlimited resources but from working within tight boundaries. The constraint forces you to think laterally, discard the obvious, and find novel pathways. History's greatest innovations often arrived when creators had the least freedom to follow convention.
cards.takeaway: When facing a creative block, artificially tighten your constraints—shorter timeframe, fewer tools, smaller budget—and watch novel ideas surface.

cards.title: Remix beats novelty
cards.insight: Truly original work rarely invents entirely new elements; instead, it recombines existing ideas in fresh configurations. The creative act lies not in the parts but in their synthesis and the perspective that reveals their unexpected harmony.
cards.takeaway: Collect and study diverse influences from outside your field; the best ideas come from unexpected collisions between distant domains.

cards.title: Failure is data, not defeat
cards.insight: Creative professionals who iterate fast and document failures learn far more than those who deliberate endlessly before attempting. Each failed attempt shrinks the solution space and teaches what doesn't work—invaluable information.
cards.takeaway: Make failure cheap and fast: prototype early, seek feedback ruthlessly, and treat each flop as a compass pointing toward what's next.

cards.title: Boredom precedes breakthroughs
cards.insight: Deep creativity requires boredom—undistracted time for the mind to wander, recombine, and find unexpected connections. The modern craving for constant stimulation starves the subconscious work that precedes genuine insight.
cards.takeaway: Schedule unstructured, stimulus-free time each week; some of your best ideas will arrive when you're not actively chasing them.

ai.title: Anthropic prices largest IPO in market history
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic prices the largest IPO in history as AI rivals close in
ai.summary: Anthropic, the AI startup founded by former OpenAI researchers, completed the largest initial public offering in market history, pricing the offering as competition intensifies in the generative AI sector. The company's strong valuation reflects investor appetite for AI infrastructure plays, though market volatility has since challenged that confidence.

ai.title: OpenAI scientist proposes AI development limits framework
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric
ai.summary: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki called for leading AI firms to voluntarily agree on development limits tied to a model intelligence metric (log-perplexity), aiming to coordinate responsible AI scaling. The proposal seeks industry-wide standards to prevent an uncontrolled race to build ever-larger models without safety guardrails.

ai.title: California sues OpenAI over safety failures
ai.feedTitle: California sues OpenAI over alleged AI safety failures
ai.summary: California filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging that the company has failed to implement adequate safety measures and safeguards for its AI models, posing public safety risks. The legal action marks an early attempt by state authorities to hold major AI firms accountable for the safety and security of their systems.

ai.title: U.S. Army partners with OpenAI for software accreditation
ai.feedTitle: Army partners with OpenAI to accelerate software accreditation
ai.summary: The U.S. Army announced a partnership with OpenAI to accelerate the accreditation and security review of military software systems. The collaboration aims to streamline the certification process for AI-augmented defense applications while maintaining rigorous security standards.

ai.title: China accessed advanced U.S. AI chips, U.S. intelligence says
ai.feedTitle: China accessed advanced US AI chips, prompting new export controls
ai.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies reported that China likely obtained restricted American AI chips, prompting new export control measures. The revelation underscores ongoing concerns about technology leakage to adversaries and complicates the geopolitical competition over AI capabilities and semiconductor supply chains.
